name: Benign Vascular Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Benign Vascular Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of a well-circumscribed, red to purple cutaneous or subcutaneous lesion
Ultrasound or MRI showing a lobulated, hypervascular mass without invasive features
Biopsy demonstrating proliferation of benign endothelial cells forming vascular channels
No evidence of cellular atypia or mitotic figures on histology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical presentation plus imaging and histopathological confirmation of benign endothelial proliferation without malignant features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and histopathology; biopsy is reserved for atypical or uncertain cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Well-demarcated red to purple cutaneous nodule

pathognomonic.notes: May increase in size with crying or Valsalva maneuver

common.notes: Often present on the head and neck region
searchTerms: localized skin redness with tiny visible blood vessels
skin discoloration with small red veins
patch of skin with visible blood vessels

common.notes: May be detected in deeper lesions

occasional.notes: May occur in rapidly growing lesions

occasional.symptomName: Functional impairment due to lesion size
occasional.notes: May affect adjacent structures depending on location
searchTerms: difficulty using area due to lesion size

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure secondary to large vascular tumor
rare.notes: Very rare, typically in large or multiple lesions
searchTerms: heart failure from large blood vessel tumor
high-output heart failure caused by vascular growth
cardiac overload due to big vascular lesion

rare.notes: Rare complication in some vascular tumors
searchTerms: low platelet count with vascular tumor

laboratory: Normal blood counts except in rare Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon with thrombocytopenia
imaging: MRI demonstrating lobulated vascular mass without invasion
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified in sporadic cases
other: Histopathology showing benign endothelial proliferation with vascular channel formation

distinguishingFeatures: Different imaging characteristics (slow flow vs high flow)
Presence of cellular atypia and mitotic figures

references: Mulliken JB, Glowacki J. Hemangiomas and vascular malformations in infants and children: a classification based on endothelial characteristics. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1982 Mar;69(3):412-22.
Enjolras O, Mulliken JB. Vascular tumors and vascular malformations (new issues). Adv Dermatol. 1997;13:375-423.
